page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance optimized for compute workloads requiring fast local scratch storage. Built on Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors running up to 4.2 GHz across 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs, it features 480 MB of shared L3 cache and supports Intel AMX along with AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is allocated 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread, alongside a dedicated 1890 GB local NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute, compression, and text parsing throughput. The platform achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2191.0 and a multi-core score of 17995.0, bolstered by high decompression performance reaching 202.24 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3. Text-oriented and lightweight inference tasks perform well, with small model text generation reaching 346.08 tokens/sec and static web serving sustaining 54.89 GB/sec. Broader system operations, such as Redis SET commands at 53.73 million operations/sec and PassMark database operations, deliver baseline average ratings.

The 1:2 memory configuration provides a cost-efficient resource profile for compute-dense applications that do not require standard 1:4 memory allocations. However, applications with significant working memory footprints may find the 64.0 GB allocation constraining. Workloads best matched to the D32lds_v7 include static web serving, high-throughput compression pipelines, Clang-based software compilation, batch text processing, and intermediate storage caching via its 1890 GB NVMe SSD.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 provides 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores driven by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, accompanied by 480 MB of L3 cache and advanced vector support including AMX and AVX-512. It features 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, and integrates a high-speed 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-quartile performance in Geekbench metrics, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 202.24 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput of 54.89 GB/sec. Its reduced memory density offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-focused architectures that do not need large RAM footprints. The D32lds_v7 is well aligned for CI/CD compilation pipelines, compression tasks, batch text processing, and caching tiers leveraging high-speed local disk storage.
